To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the oligonucleotidic derivative pT16 is a useful tool for studying the interaction between nucleic acid and mammalian cells; (b) the alkylating derivative of the oligonucleoside pT16 is an effective reagent for affinity modification of the proteins interacting with oligonucletides; (c) the 83 kDA protein of the BALB/c mouse liver cell line is a receptor for oligonucleotids.

(i) alkylating derivatives (pT)15 and (pT)18 interact with the 83 kDA protein in BALB/c mouse liver cells; (ii) the interaction is specific, i.e. it is inhibited by the corresponding phosphorothioate oligomer; and (iii) the interaction is reversible and can be inhibited by the excess of unlabelled oligonucleotide.
